data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's 'counterfactual trace' is structurally incapable of distinguishing genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that tracks the right answer. A 'critical pivot' where a checklist item contradicted the panel's bias documents that the checklist causally drove the correct answer for that instance—but it does not establish a reliability GAIN over an expert, nor does it rule out compliance tracking. The target's own countercondition concedes the pivot could be coincidental (item checked but not actually used), yet the method offers no mechanism to separate a genuine reliability gain from that coincidence within a single evaluation. Worse, even a genuine pivot only proves the checklist rescued one case; it says nothing about whether the panel is MORE reliable than a single expert on average. The claim conflates 'the checklist caused the correct answer here' with 'the panel is more reliable on average,' which is the very conflation the problem asks to disentangle.
